workflows.note: The repository's required workflow, declared in .github-delivery/ci-policy.json. The local command runs the same gates against the same eight generated projections; it does not run under the hosted image, the workflow token, or the artifact service.
Deterministic queue check with a selftest. The local and hosted commands are the same argv, which is what makes this entry a cheap comparison rather than an approximate one.
Module test runner. Its physical control group spawns subprocesses, so a local pass and a hosted pass can genuinely differ on process behaviour -- which is the case worth comparing.
Module test runner. The job name and the module name differ here on purpose: the index maps to the job the workflow declares, not to the name a reader would guess.

Console projection, bounded views and the signed request path. Its physical control spawns subprocesses and reads HITL_SIGNER_KEY from the environment, so the local and hosted runs genuinely differ in what is configured -- which is why the unset-key case is part of the control rather than something CI papers over.

The one workflow whose local and hosted runs are expected to differ in what they measure and not just in where: the module's own contract forbids CI from publishing a timing number, so CI runs the synthetic lane and the real measurement stays LOCAL.
